title: Spark instances go live before the RRC Framework is fully implemented for them
content:
The first slot in every Instance Configuration Document is `RRC Framework Full Implementation`, and its value is a bare status. The Avalanche Spark Savings v2 USDC instance reads **`Covered`** (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.1). The Robinhood Chain USDG instance (.3.5.1.1.1) and the X Layer USDT instance (.3.6.1.1.1) both read **`Pending`** — while carrying supply caps of 500,000,000 USDG and 750,000,000 USDT respectively.

Both `Pending` instances are nevertheless filed under headings declaring that instances "with `Active` Status are stored herein."

This is a tension the Artifact records rather than resolves. Making RRC coverage the *first* field of every instance is a deliberate transparency choice: the gap is impossible to miss and trivially auditable across the whole portfolio. But surfacing the gap is not the same as gating on it — nothing in the structure prevents an uncovered instance from being active, and the Completed-status Blackrock (.4.1.1.1), Centrifuge (.4.2.1.1) and Morpho (.4.3.1.1.1) instances are *also* `Pending`, meaning some integrations ran their entire lifecycle without full framework coverage.

The honest reading: RRC implementation is a retrofit programme running behind an already-deployed portfolio, and the Artifact is the ledger of how far behind.
description: Instances carrying 500M–750M supply caps are filed under Active Status with RRC Framework Full Implementation marked Pending, so risk-framework coverage lags capital deployment.
